facts.statement: Gnathovorax lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic, Carnian

facts.statement: Gnathovorax fossils were found in the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: Gnathovorax is a genus of herrerasaurid saurischian dinosaur from the Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.

facts.statement: The only known species, Gnathovorax cabreirai, was described by Pacheco and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Gnathovorax cabreirai, described by Pacheco et al. in 2019.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 2014 at the Marchezan site in São João do Polêsine, Brazil.
facts.quote: It was found in 2014 at the Marchezan site, in the municipality of São João do Polêsine, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.

facts.statement: The geological layer containing the fossils is dated to approximately 233.23 million years ago.
facts.quote: Stratigraphically correlated beds from a nearby site were dated as the middle of the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, circa 233.23 ± 0.73 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus name Gnathovorax means "voracious jaw" in Greek and Latin.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek gnathos, jaw, and the Latin vorax, "voracious", from vorō ("devour") + −āx ("inclined to").

facts.statement: The species name cabreirai honors Dr. Sérgio Furtado Cabreira, who discovered the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific epithet was given in honour of Dr. Sérgio Furtado Cabreira, the palaeontologist who found the specimen.

facts.statement: The type specimen is a nearly complete, well-preserved skeleton found alongside rhynchosaurs and cynodonts.
facts.quote: The type specimen comprises a mostly complete and well-preserved articulated skeleton (considered one of the best herrerasaurid skeletons ever discovered), which fossilized in close association with rhynchosaur and cynodont remains.

facts.statement: Gnathovorax had three teeth in its premaxilla, whereas Herrerasaurus had four.
facts.quote: There were three teeth in the premaxilla, in contrast to Herrerasaurus (which possessed four).

facts.statement: Its teeth were thin, curved, and blade-like, with serrations on the rear and front edges of the upper teeth.
facts.quote: The 3 premaxillary, 19 maxillary, and 14 dentary teeth are all thin, curved, and blade-like.

facts.statement: The top of the braincase had a trapezoidal shape with a blade-like crest, unlike the triangular shape of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: The supraoccipital bone at the top of the braincase is trapezoidal when seen from behind (unlike Herrerasaurus's triangular supraoccipital) and has a blade-like crest on top.

facts.statement: Gnathovorax is the only herrerasaurid with a scapula that curves backward, has an expanded tip, and is not fused to the coracoid.
facts.quote: Gnathovorax is the only herrerasaurid combining features of the scapula such as posterior curvature, an expanded tip, and no fusion with the coracoid.

facts.statement: The ischium possessed a hole at its base called an obturator foramen, a feature shared with lagerpetids but not other herrerasaurids.
facts.quote: Unlike other herrerasaurids (but like lagerpetids), the ischium has a hole known as an obturator foramen at its base.

facts.statement: The fifth toe of the foot had three phalanges, unlike Herrerasaurus which had only one.
facts.quote: The foot has three phalanges (toe bone) in the fifth toe, while Herrerasaurus only has one.

facts.statement: A 2022 CT scan revealed that Gnathovorax lacked an invasive air sac system and had non-pneumatized bones.
facts.quote: In 2022, Aureliano and colleagues performed a mirco-computed tomography scan on the postcranial skeletons of some of the earliest saurischian dinosaurs that lived during the late Carnian including Gnathovorax with sauropodomorphs Pampadromaeus and Buriolestes, which showed that the invasive air sac system was absent and that their bones were not pneumatised.

facts.statement: Researchers reconstructed a digital endocast of the brain from the well-preserved holotype skeleton.
facts.quote: The holotype skeleton of Gnathovorax is so well preserved that its describers were able to reconstruct a digital endocast of the brain.

facts.statement: The brain contained a large floccular fossa lobe, which is generally associated with motor control of the eyes, head, and neck.
facts.quote: It possessed a large floccular fossa lobe (FFL) of the cerebellum, a portion of the brain generally (but not universally) considered useful for motor control of the eye, head, and neck.

facts.statement: Most paleontologists interpret the large floccular fossa lobe as evidence of an active predatory lifestyle.
facts.quote: These features mean that most paleontologists consider a large FFL to be indicative of an active predatory lifestyle, explaining why it is reduced in later sauropodomorphs but not in most theropods.

facts.statement: Lesions on the skull suggest the animal engaged in intraspecific combat involving face biting or claw raking.
facts.quote: The skull of a G. cabreirai specimen displays craniofacial lesions that were most likely caused by intraspecific combat in the form of either face biting or claw raking.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Gnathovorax in a polytomy with Herrerasaurus and Sanjuansaurus within the family Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Within Herrerasauridae, Gnathovorax was found in a polytomy with Herrerasaurus and Sanjuansaurus.

facts.statement: Some analyses argue that Herrerasauridae, including Gnathovorax, are basal Saurischians outside the Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: The paper describing Gnathovorax contained a cladistic analysis which argued that the Herrerasauridae are basal Saurischia, outside of the Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha.
